purpose: Default Mars scenario with a brighter fixed camera exposure for the Belva test levels; not calibrated site photometry
dust_spectral_model: Grey RGB approximation to an 880 nm scenario opacity; no measured wavelength conversion or phase function
provenance: Radius follows the DEM reference body. Gas scale height 11 km and Sun distance use nominal NASA values. Tau880=0.45 is a scenario inside a published early Jezero range of 0.4-0.5, not a chosen sol measurement. Grey SSA=0.93 is a scenario motivated by TES solar-band fits of 0.92-0.94, not a Jezero spectral retrieval. Dust height=11 km is an assumed exponential profile, independently configurable from gas. RGB Rayleigh values, anisotropy, terrain colour, 30 klux, exposure and sun pose remain uncalibrated. No Earth ozone layer, extra fog, synthetic collision rocks or fabricated relief. A single grey Henyey-Greenstein aerosol cannot validate Mars sky colours or its blue sunset aureole. Exposure EV100 10 was chosen from PIE grabs on BelvaLab01 and BelvaRockLab01 (2026-11-26, sun 35 deg at azimuth 135 deg, four rover headings): at EV100 13 the navigation cameras showed 86-99% of ground pixels below 10/255; at EV100 10 ground medians were 95-114/255 with no pixel at or above 250. Shadowed rock faces stayed mostly black at EV100 10. Valid only for this sun and terrain; not a camera calibration.
